data_fields.name: queue_link_cap
data_fields.donor_constant: 2 links per queue tile (cap at 767; spare-link test at 496)

best_idea: A path tile joins its neighbours in a fixed priority order (entrance first, then a queue with a spare link, then a plain path), and a queue tile keeps at most two links, so a service line never grows into a junction.
decision_why: The priority-then-cap rule suits zone paths between hubs (a hub entrance joins first, a walkway never becomes a four-way crossing); the ride, queue-chain and park-entrance specifics are RCT2 park rules and are rejected. The donor's index-skip defect in the queue filter is fixed in the sketch.
acceptance: A zone-authoring test lays out one hub entrance and four neighbouring plain-path tiles and asserts the entrance link is made first, that a queue-type path tile never has more than two links after a rebuild, and that a second hub's queue beside the first is not joined to the first hub's ride.
